---
title: "Contributing to JAXCMR"
---

The Python source lives in `jaxcmr/` and the tests in `tests/`. If you’re
editing something readers see on the website, your starting point might be a
Python docstring, a guide page, or a template notebook.

## Set up a checkout {#prepare-the-environment}

A checkout is your local copy of the repository. Open a terminal in its
top-level folder, the one containing `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`.
If you still need a copy, follow the [checkout instructions](developer-setup.ipynb#optional-repository-checkout).
Run the commands on this page from that folder.

```bash
uv sync --locked --extra test --group reader --group docs
```

`uv sync` prepares a Python environment in `.venv` and installs JAXCMR
from your checkout. The next time you start Python in that environment, it
uses your edited source. Syncing can remove packages outside the selection
from an existing environment.

- `--locked` uses the package versions recorded in `uv.lock`. If the lockfile
  needs updating, uv stops and tells you.
- `--extra test` includes pytest, the program that runs the library tests.
- `--group reader` adds tools for running and checking notebooks.
- `--group docs` adds the Python tools for generating the API reference.
  To render web pages, also install [Quarto 1.11.9](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/tag/v1.11.9).

## Change and test the library

The serial position curve answers a question about each study position.
What fraction of the items presented there were recalled? The calculation is
`spc` in `jaxcmr/analyses/spc.py`. Its tests are in
`tests/test_recall_measures.py`. Run them once before editing so you know
which checks already pass.

```bash
uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests/test_recall_measures.py
```

`uv run --no-sync` uses the environment you just prepared and skips the
installation step. `python -m pytest` starts pytest with that environment’s
Python. The path selects one test file. At the end, pytest reports how many
tests passed or failed. For a failure, it shows the test name and the
comparison that failed.

Give your change a test whose expected result you can work out by hand.
Suppose the study lists are `[A, B, A]` and `[C, D]`. The participant
recalls A twice on the first trial and nothing on the second. Each position
where A was studied gets credit once. The recall fractions for positions 1,
2, and 3 are **1/2, 0/2, and 1/1**. Only the first list contributes to the
third denominator. In the test file, look for
`test_position_codes_recall_all_presentations_without_double_counting` to
see how a similar list and its expected scores are written in Python.
Run the same test command after editing the function and its test.

If you change how the experimental CMR fitters prepare observations, run
`uv run --no-sync python -m pytest -m audit`. Here `-m audit` selects the
tests that check whether JAX can reuse a compiled calculation when the
selected trials change.

## Edit notebooks and documentation

### Change a notebook

To change the category recall rate template, open
`templates/cat_recall_rate.ipynb`. Tutorial and Library Guide notebooks
live in `guide/tutorials/` and `guide/overview/`. If you change a
calculation, select the checkout’s Python environment as the notebook kernel,
run the cells, and save the output you want readers to see. For a text-only edit, the existing output can stay.

You can then test the saved template from the terminal.

```bash
uv run --no-sync python guide/tools/check_notebooks.py --select cat_recall_rate
```

The script runs a temporary copy with a small workload and checks its results.
Your original keeps the settings and output you saved. The script prints
the path to a report showing which notebooks passed. `--select` picks one
notebook by its name, such as `cat_recall_rate`. Omit it to run the whole collection.

### Change an API reference entry

Suppose you’re clarifying the entry for `simulate_dataset`. Edit the
description inside that function in `jaxcmr/simulation.py` (its *docstring*).
The docstring at the top of the module supplies the page introduction.
To add an entry or move it under a different heading, edit the list in
`guide/reference/_simulation.yml`.

```bash
quarto render guide/reference/simulation.qmd
```

This rebuilds the simulation reference page. In the local website preview,
open **API Reference → Memory models → Simulation** and follow the function’s link in the summary table.

### Change an input supplied with the package

If a notebook uses one of JAXCMR’s bundled datasets or saved fits, edit the
source file under `data/`. For a new file, also add its path to
`_EXAMPLE_FILES` in `jaxcmr/examples.py`, so `copy_example_inputs` recognizes
it, and to the wheel and source-archive file lists in `pyproject.toml`, so
it ships with the package.

Add `--reinstall-package jaxcmr` to the setup command above to refresh the
installed copy of the data. Rerun the notebook that reads it. To check that
someone installing the package also receives the file, run
`uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests/test_distribution.py`. These tests
build and install the package in a fresh environment and need internet access
for dependencies.

### Preview and share your change

The website’s theme, navigation, and default code controls are set in
`guide/_quarto.yml`. Edit `guide/styles.scss` for layout shared by light and
dark mode. The palette files supply colors. Command-oriented pages use
`guide/_commands.yml` to show commands without line numbers. Formatting
specific to API entries lives in `guide/reference/reference.css`.

The API sidebar also supplies the group names and links for the homepage and
reference index. Edit the page descriptions in `guide/reference/index.qmd`.

Published notebooks carry a copy of their code controls so readers can render a
download on its own. After changing those defaults, run
`uv run --no-sync python guide/prepare.py --sync-notebook-format` to refresh
those settings in the notebook sources.

After changing shared styling or navigation, build the whole site. Quarto embeds
the sidebar in each page, so a single-page render updates only one copy.

```bash
bash build-docs.sh
uv run --no-sync python guide/tools/check_site.py docs
uv run --no-sync python -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory docs
```

The first command builds the site in `docs/` using the outputs already
saved in the notebooks. The second checks local links, notebook downloads,
and example files. The third serves the built pages at
[`http://127.0.0.1:8000/`](http://127.0.0.1:8000/), where the browser can
load Quarto’s navigation scripts. Press **Ctrl+C** in the terminal to stop the server. To inspect a revised notebook, use its download link.
**Open in Colab** opens the version on GitHub’s `main` branch.

To propose a code or documentation change, open a pull request asking to
merge the edits on your branch into JAXCMR. If you’re working in your own
copy on GitHub, follow [GitHub’s instructions for submitting from a fork](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/create-pull-requests/creating-a-pull-request-from-a-fork).
Describe what will change for readers or researchers and how you checked it.
GitHub runs the routine library tests on Linux, macOS, and Windows and
checks the website build. The notebook runner and the clean-install
tests run locally, so include their results if you ran them.
